title: In re Richard Braithwaite, Case No. 26-037C (Carlin City Manager)
text:
STATEOFNEVADA
BEFORETHENEVADACOMMISSIONONETHICS
In re Richard Braithwaite, Ethics Complaint
City Manager, City of Carlin, Case No. 26-037C
State of Nevada,
Subject. /
STIPULATED AGREEMENT
1. PURPOSE: This Stipulated Agreement resolves Ethics Complaint, Case
No. 26-037C (“Complaint”) before the Nevada Commission on Ethics (“Commission”)
concerning Richard Braithwaite (“Braithwaite”), City Manager for the City of Carlin (“City”).
2. JURISDICTION: At all material times, Braithwaite served as the City
Manager for the City and was a public officer as defined in NRS 281A.160. The Ethics in
Government Law (“Ethics Law”) set forth in NRS Chapter 281A gives the Commission
jurisdiction over elected and appointed public officers and public employees whose
conduct is alleged to have violated the provisions of NRS Chapter 281A. See NRS
281A.280. The Commission has jurisdiction over Braithwaite in this matter.
3. PROCEDURAL HISTORY BEFORE COMMISSION
a. On or about February 2, 2026, the Commission received Ethics Complaint 26-
037C from a member of the public, alleging violations ofNRS 281A.400(1), (2),
and (7).
b. Upon review of the allegations and publicly available information, Commission
staff determined that the allegations may additionally implicate NRS
281A.400(9).
c. On March 19, 2026, the Commission accepted jurisdiction and issued its Order
on Jurisdiction and Investigation, directing the Executive Director to investigate
the matter and serve Braithwaite with notice of the investigation and the
allegations against him.
Stipulated Agreement

d. On March 23, 2026, pursuant to NRS 281A.720 and NAC 281A.410, staff of
the Commission served Braithwaite with Notice of Complaint, Additional Issues
and Facts, and Investigation regarding the alleged violations of NRS
281A.400(1), (2), (7) and (9) and provided Braithwaite with an opportunity to
respond to the allegations.
e. On or about April 20, 2026, Braithwaite provided a written response to the
Complaint.
f. Braithwaite and the Executive Director, through counsel, engaged in
discussions pertaining to an early resolution.
g. Braithwaite has waived the Ethics Law requirement of a Review Panel to enter
into this Stipulated Agreement.
h. In lieu of an adjudicatory hearing before the Commission, Braithwaite and the
Commission now enter into this Stipulated Agreement.
4. STIPULATED FACTS: At all material times, the following facts were
relevant to this matter:1
a. Braithwaite served as the City Manager for the City during all material times
and was therefore a public officer pursuant to NRS 281A.160.
b. As City Manager, Braithwaite directly oversaw City departments and
department heads, including the Public Works Department and its former
Director, Joe Massa (“Massa”).
c. The City’s Public Works Department maintains City vehicles and equipment
through a City-owned maintenance shop staffed by City employees during
working hours.
d. During the relevant period, the City employed Brian Grondin (“Grondin”) as its
mechanic to perform maintenance and repair work on City vehicles and
equipment.
e. In October of 2025, Braithwaite discussed with Massa the ongoing mechanical
issues he was experiencing with his personal Ford F-150 truck.
1 Stipulated Facts do not constitute part of the “Investigative File” as that term is defined by NRS 281A.775.
All statutory and common law protections afforded to the Investigative File shall remain and are not affected
by this Stipulated Agreement.
Stipulated Agreement

f. Massa thereafter directed Grondin to inspect Braithwaite’s personal vehicle
and perform the needed repairs.
g. On or about October 16 and 17, 2025, Grondin performed brake and rotor
repair work on Braithwaite’s truck at the City maintenance shop during working
hours using City facilities and equipment.
h. The replacement parts used during the repair were not purchased through the
City but were acquired through Grondin’s private business account using funds
advanced by Massa. The replacement parts associated with the repairs totaled
approximately $381.68 after Grondin’s private business discount was applied
to the purchase.
i. Braithwaite paid for the replacement parts associated with the repairs but did
not reimburse the City for labor associated with the work at the time the repairs
were completed.
j. Grondin estimated the repair work required approximately one and one-half to
two hours of labor and stated that he charges approximately $100 per hour for
similar work through his private business.
k. The City has no policy or employment provision authorizing the City Manager
to utilize City mechanic services, facilities, or labor for repairs to a personal
vehicle.
l. On April 8, 2026, Braithwaite submitted his resignation from the City Manager
position and stated his intended final day of employment would be May 29,
2026.
m. Braithwaite cooperated with the Commission’s investigation, waived the
statutory investigation and review panel time requirements pursuant to NRS
281A.725, and engaged in settlement discussions through counsel regarding
resolution of this matter.
5. TERMS / CONCLUSIONS OF LAW: Based on the foregoing, Braithwaite and the
Commission agree as follows:
a. Each of the stipulated facts enumerated in Section 4 of this Stipulated
Agreement is agreed to by the parties.
b. Braithwaite was a public officer as defined in NRS 281A.160.
Stipulated Agreement
Case No. 26-037C
Page 3 of 7

c. Braithwaite’s actions constitute a single course of conduct resulting in one
willful violation of the Ethics Law, implicating the provisions of NRS
281A.400(7) (prohibited the use of governmental time, property, equipment or
other facility to benefit a significant personal or pecuniary interest). See e.g. In
re Pamintuan, Comm’n Op. No. 25-159C (2025); In re Antinoro, Comm’n Op.
No. 17-21C (2019); In re Boldt, Comm’n Op. No. 17-37C (2017).
d. Allegations that Braithwaite violated NRS 281A.400(1), (2), and (9) are hereby
dismissed as part of the negotiated resolution of this matter.
e. Based upon the consideration and application of the statutory mitigating and
aggravating circumstances set forth in NRS 281A.775, the Commission
concludes that the following resolution is appropriate:
1) Braithwaite has not previously been the subject of any violation of the
Ethics Law.
2) Braithwaite recognizes that City resources and employee labor should not
have been utilized in connection with repairs to his personal vehicle.
3) Braithwaite paid for the replacement parts associated with the repairs.
4) Braithwaite cooperated with the Commission’s investigation and
resolution of this matter.
5) The conduct nevertheless resulted in the use of City facilities, equipment,
and employee labor during working hours for the benefit of Braithwaite’s
personal pecuniary interest.
6) Braithwaite has since resigned from his position as City Manager.
f. Braithwaite agrees to pay restitution in the amount of $200 to the City and
provide the Executive Director with proof of payment within sixty (60) days of
approval of this stipulation.
g. Braithwaite agrees to pay a civil penalty pursuant to NRS 281A.790 in the
amount of $200 within sixty (60) days of approval of this stipulation.
h. This order serves as an admonishment, an written expression of disapproval
of Braithwaite’s conduct, pursuant to NRS 281A.785
Stipulated Agreement

i. This Stipulated Agreement is based on the specific facts, circumstances, and
law now before the Commission. Facts or circumstances that differ from those
present in this matter may create a different resolution.
j. This Agreement is intended to apply to and resolve only this specific proceeding
before the Commission and is not intended to be applicable to or create any
admission of liability for any other proceeding, including administrative, civil, or
criminal, regarding Braithwaite. If the Commission rejects this Stipulated
Agreement, none of the provisions herein shall be considered by the
Commission or be admissible as evidence in a hearing on the merits in this
matter.
6. WAIVER
Braithwaite knowingly and voluntarily waives his right to a hearing before the
a.
full Commission on the allegations in Ethics Complaint Case No. 26-037C and
all rights he may be accorded with regard to this matter pursuant to NRS
Chapter 281A, the regulations of the Commission (NAC Chapter 281A), the
Nevada Administrative Procedures Act (NRS Chapter 233B) and any other
applicable provisions of law.
Braithwaite knowingly and voluntarily waives his right to any judicial review of
b.
this matter as provided in NRS Chapter 281A, NRS Chapter 233B or any other
applicable provisions of law.
7. ACCEPTANCE: We, the undersigned parties, have read this Stipulated
Agreement, understand each and every provision therein, and agree to be bound thereby.
The parties orally agreed to be bound by the terms of this agreement during the regular
meeting of the Commission on June 17, 2026.2
